correctness.rationale: Rejecting a mask using a Jacobian zero over an extension field is sound but does not certify the survivors. I instead partitioned all 65,535 nonzero coefficient masks into 1,075 orbits, without using the frozen finite-field sieve, and applied exact Jacobian unit-ideal tests over F₂ on the four standard affine charts. The independently computed 16,020 smooth masks and all 252 representative rows match the frozen files exactly, as do all rational-point bins, stabilizer orders, and the 25 incidence-pattern counts. Smooth (3,3) divisors are geometrically connected by the divisor exact sequence and Künneth, hence geometrically integral. Adjunction gives K=O(1,1)|C; the four sections restrict isomorphically, and the Segre map is canonical. Any second containing quadric would restrict to a section of O(−1,−1) after imposing vanishing on C, and hence vanish identically on the first quadric. Isomorphisms thus extend to automorphisms of the same split quadric, whose action is generated by the two six-element linear groups and factor exchange. Conversely a smooth genus-four canonical curve on that quadric has type (a,b) with a+b=6 and (a−1)(b−1)=4, hence (3,3). The eight-point orbit has size 36 and stabilizer order 2.
residual_risks: Correctness covers the smooth split locus only, not other quadrics, hyperelliptic curves or other fields.

evidence: The algorithm fixes each quadric, quotients cubic equations by multiples of q and the projective stabilizer, tests nonsingularity and records the defining pair and point vector.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Select q₁ rows and substitute Segre coordinates into each cubic. Every nonzero F₂ section has a unique scalar normalization. For each row, checking the 72 transformations gives the orbit size and stabilizer. Evaluating the nine rational grid points gives the binary incidence mask; canonicalize it under the same group and accumulate with orbit-size weights. This is a direct database computation without new geometric smoothness or isomorphism classification. A statement that the prior paper literally prints all those bins is not needed or made.

originality.rationale: Xarles already performs a complete genus-four classification over F₂, explicitly including the split quadric and giving complete defining equations by canonical quadric and point counts in the supplement. The joint section/class/stabilizer tables and the 25 incidence bins are not asserted to be printed there. They are mechanical filters and tabulations of the classified equations: filter the split normal form, pull back by Segre, loop over the 72 transformations and evaluate nine points. Distinct same-day Resultary findings also state the same smooth-family totals for different invariants. The omission of the stronger census from the frozen priority analysis is material.
residual_risks: The prior author list was not reprocessed in full. The decisive evidence is the published exhaustive construction and form of the equation-level dataset, not an assertion that all frozen tables had already been printed.

value.rationale: The split locus is mathematically natural and a checked re-tabulation may be convenient. Here the stated quantities only filter and weight a complete existing list and evaluate its models at nine fixed points; the record does not establish a distinct nonmechanical incidence result. The certified recomputation by itself does not meet the scientific-value requirement for a new exact invariant.
residual_risks: No judgment is made against the underlying census, the utility of a compact table, or a future structural theorem about the pattern counts.
